A.explanation: The lighter skater moves right at $1.4 \text{m s}^{-1}$ while the heavier moves right at $0.80 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so separation speed is $1.4 - 0.80 = 0.6 \text{m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is the velocity of the $40 \text{ kg}$ skater after collision to the right, not the relative speed between the two skaters.

C.explanation: This adds $1.4 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $0.80 \text{m s}^{-1}$ as if the skaters move in opposite directions after collision, but both move to the right.

D.explanation: This treats the $40 \text{ kg}$ skater as rebounding to the left, giving $1.4 + 0.80$ separation, which violates conservation of total momentum.

hints: Take right as positive: the $80 \text{ kg}$ skater has $+2.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the $40 \text{ kg}$ skater has $-1.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ before collision.
Use conservation of total momentum to find the unknown velocity of the $40 \text{ kg}$ skater after the $80 \text{ kg}$ skater slows to $+0.80 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Relative speed of separation is the magnitude of the difference of the two velocities after collision, noting both end up moving to the right.
walkthrough: Choose positive direction to the right. Before: $p = m_1u_1 + m_2u_2 = (80)(+2.0) + (40)(-1.0) = 160 - 40 = 120 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
After collision let the $40 \text{ kg}$ velocity be $v_2$. Then $p = (80)(+0.80) + 40v_2 = 64 + 40v_2$.
Conserve momentum: $64 + 40v_2 = 120$, so $40v_2 = 56$ and $v_2 = +1.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The lighter skater therefore moves to the right faster than the heavier skater.
Relative speed of separation is $|v_2 - v_1| = |1.4 - 0.80| = 0.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with units of speed. This is option A.
